subject: How to add spike histograms to multiple curves

messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: How to add spike histograms to multiple curves
parts:
I have several service functions in the Hmisc package that I'd like to translate to layer functions in ggplot2.  Two of them are scat1d and histSpike.  I have found that spike histograms are better than rug plots for large datasets and want to start with histSpike.  [A spike histogram uses thin lines to indicate relative counts using either unique x values occurring in the data or 100 bins whichever is less and with vertical line lengths proportional to counts, with maximum height of about 0.3 cm.  Spike histograms are effective where there are many curves, even if they intertwine.]  Here is an example goal:

  1. From data frame A draw two curves (x, y) distinguished by color indicating groups (e.g., female/male).
  2. Compute x values and relative counts for each value of the grouping variable and store them in data frame B (which has 3 variables).
  3. Along each curve drawn in step 1 add the spike histograms using geom_segment() with the vertical segments centered on the curve values (curves are linearly interpolated for this purpose using approx()).  Spikes should be the same color as used for the group variable in step 1.
Any guidance about which attack to use would be appreciated.  I know how to do this when ggplot(aes(...)) does not include the group variable.

As an aside I could not see how to use physical units of measurements with geom_segment for heights of segments.  I guess I need to use something like y range/50 using ggplot_build(ggplot2 object) [I don't know how to sense the y-axis range when the ggplot2 object is not yet complete].

Here is an example:

require(Hmisc)
set.seed(1)
x <- seq(0, 1, by=0.01)
y1 <- x + x^2
y2 <- x - 2*x^3 + 1
plot(x, y1, type='l')
lines(x, y2)
xs <- rnorm(1000, .3, .3)
xs2 <- rnorm(1000, .7, .3)
histSpike(xs, curve=list(x=x, y=y1), add=TRUE)
histSpike(xs2, curve=list(x=x, y=y2), add=TRUE)



Thanks
Frank

messages.subject: Re: How to add spike histograms to multiple curves
parts:
This seems to work out of the box once I fixed a programming error.  Here is an example.  I just wish there were a way to use physical dimensions with geom_segment and to sense xlim and ylim in effect so I could remove data out of bounds and so I can scale the tick marks more easily.  -Frank

require(ggplot2)
set.seed(1)
ints   <- c(a=.04, b=.4,  c=.6)
slopes <- c(a=.5,  b=1.1, c=.9)
incr   <- c(a=.01, b=.02, c=.03)
p <- function(x, g, z='point') {
  y <- ints[g] + slopes[g] * x
  switch(z,
         point = y,
         low   = y - incr[g],
         hi    = y + incr[g])
}

d <- expand.grid(g=c('a','b','c'), x=c(0,1))
d$y <- with(d, p(x, g))
g <- ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, color=g)) + geom_line()
f <- data.frame(g=sample(c('a','b','c'), 50, TRUE),
                x=runif(50))
f$low <- with(f, p(x, g, 'low'))
f$hi  <- with(f, p(x, g, 'hi'))
g + geom_segment(data=f, aes(x=x, xend=x, y=low, yend=hi))

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: How to add spike histograms to multiple curves
parts:
Hi Frank:

I took a quick look at histSpike() and it's pretty clear from its return value that you can't pass it directly to ggplot() :) 

ggplot2:: stat_bin() is known to be wonky when it comes to computing relative frequencies on a groupwise basis so I wouldn't completely trust it if you want to be able to support counts, proportions and densities. You're better off writing a function to set up the data in a form that is easily passed to ggplot() which you did in your example. I think if you rewrote histSpikes() to return a data frame or list of data frames that you could pass to ggplot() directly, you'd have better luck. 

From what I saw, it looks like histSpikes() determines the axis limits inside the function body. You can take advantage of that to make one data frame for the curves, perhaps another for the x location, top and bottom of the spikes and a third for the limits and return them as a list. The graph could be produced with a function that takes the list as one input argument with others as necessary and then assign them to different data frames inside the function. One of the advantages of ggplot2 is that you can use different data frames to produce different layers and this approach would give you complete control over the contents of the graphic.

To set axis limits, you can use xlim()/ylim() or the limits = argument of scale_(x/y)_continuous(). In the case I'm envisioning, the data frame for the limits would have one line and you could use DF$var to access individual values.

My impression is that you already do the necessary computations in histSpikes() so it's just a matter of organizing the output so that it's easy to pass to ggplot(). 

Cheers,
Dennis

messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Re: How to add spike histograms to multiple curves
parts:
Hi Dennis,

Thanks for your thoughts.  I've put together a function that seems to be working - code is below preceded by example usage.  I'm addding histSpikeg to the Hmisc package.

f <- lrm(y ~ blood.pressure + sex * (age + rcs(cholesterol,4)),
         data=d)
p <- Predict(f, cholesterol, sex)
g <- ggplot(p, aes(x=cholesterol, y=yhat, color=sex)) + geom_line() +geom_ribbon(data=p, aes(ymin=lower, ymax=upper), alpha=0.2,
                linetype=0, show_guide=FALSE)
g
g + histSpikeg(yhat ~ cholesterol + sex, p, d, ylim=c(-1, 1.25))

histSpikeg <- function(formula=NULL, predictions=NULL, data,
                       xlim=NULL, ylim=NULL,
                       side=1, nint=100, frac=.02) {
  ## Raw data in data, predicted curves are in predictions
  ## If predictions is not given, side (1 or 3) is used
  v  <- all.vars(formula)
  yv <- v[ 1]
  xv <- v[-1]
  if(length(xv) > 2) stop('may not specify more than two predictors')
  if(length(xv) == 2 && ! length(predictions))
    stop('predictions must be given if formula has two variables on the right')
  x1 <- data[[xv[1]]]
  if(length(xlim)) {
    data <- data[x1 >= xlim[1] & x1 <= xlim[2], ]
    x1 <- data[[xv[1]]]
  }
  if(length(unique(x1)) > nint) {
    eps <- diff(range(x1, na.rm=TRUE)) / nint
    x1  <- round(x1 / eps) * eps
  }
  x2 <- if(length(xv) == 2) data[[xv[2]]]
  p  <- predictions
  if(length(p)) xr <- range(p[[xv[1]]], na.rm=TRUE)
  else frac <- frac * 2
  
  if(length(xv) == 1) {
    tab    <- as.data.frame(table(x1))
    tab$x1 <- as.numeric(as.character(tab$x1))
    tab    <- tab[tab$x1 >= xr[1] & tab$x1 <= xr[2], ]
    tab$rf <- tab$Freq / sum(tab$Freq)
    if(length(p)) tab$yy <- approx(p[[xv]], p[[yv]], xout=tab$x1)$y
  } else {
    tab <- as.data.frame(table(x1, x2))
    tab <- subset(tab, Freq > 0)
    tab$x1 <- as.numeric(as.character(tab$x1))
    tab    <- tab[tab$x1 >= xr[1] & tab$x1 <= xr[2], ]
    tab$rf <- tab$Freq / sum(tab$Freq)
    tab$yy <- rep(NA, nrow(tab))
    for(s in levels(tab$x2)) {
      i <- tab$x2 == s
      j <- p[[xv[2]]] == s
      tab$yy[i] <- approx(p[[xv[1]]][j], p[[yv]][j], xout=tab$x1[i])$y
    }
  }
  tab$rf <- tab$rf * diff(ylim) * frac / max(tab$rf)
  n <- nrow(tab)
  tab$ylo <- if(length(p)) tab$yy - tab$rf
  else if(side == 1) rep(ylim[1], n) else rep(ylim[2], n)

  tab$yhi <- if(length(p)) tab$yy + tab$rf
  else if(side == 1) ylim[1] + tab$rf else ylim[2] - tab$rf
  if(length(xv) == 2) names(tab)[names(tab) == 'x2'] <- xv[2]
  
  ggplot2::geom_segment(data=tab,
                        aes(x=x1, xend=x1,
                            y=ylo, yend=yhi))
}
